name: AEI Healthcare Portfolio VII DST
description:
AEI Healthcare Portfolio VII DST is a $50.50 million, debt-free healthcare portfolio of three newly built, 100%-occupied freestanding facilities: an HonorHealth emergency room and urgent-care clinic in Surprise, Arizona; a Texas Children's medical office in Austin, Texas; and a UnitedHealthcare/ProHealth medical office in Bristol, Connecticut. The properties total approximately 51,215 rentable square feet.

The Trust leases the portfolio to an AEI affiliate under a 10-year Master Lease, with one five-year extension option. The Master Tenant pays fixed rent beginning at $2.532 million annually; projected Trust cash flow starts at 5.00% and reaches 6.14% in Year 10. A future 721 contribution is available only if both the Holder and Trust Manager elect the exchange; otherwise the FMV option pays cash.
notes:
The lack of mortgage debt reduces balance-sheet risk, but the key credit is the affiliated Master Tenant rather than the healthcare occupiers alone. The Master Tenant is newly formed, capitalized by a $500,000 demand note from AEI Trust Advisors that AEI Capital Corporation guarantees. The PPM states AEI and its affiliates have limited capital and no obligation to fund Master Lease shortfalls from other sources. This is a limited-credit Master Lease, not a corporate guaranty of the projected 5.00%-6.14% cash-flow schedule.

The portfolio combines new healthcare facilities with tenant concentration: Bristol represents 44.15% of Trust purchase price, Surprise 31.90%, and Austin 23.95%. The Master Lease captures property upside for the Master Tenant while the Trust bears specified Trust obligations and must depend on a Springing LLC if the Master Tenant defaults. The 721 route is not an investor-controlled liquidity right; it requires Trust Manager action and a Holder election.

name: AX Diversified Retail Portfolio DST
description:
AX Diversified Retail Portfolio, DST holds six single-tenant net-leased retail properties totaling approximately 668,521 net rentable square feet across five states: two Kroger stores in Muncie and Indianapolis, Indiana; a Sam's Club in Dallas, Texas; a BJ's Wholesale Club in Jacksonville, Florida; and Lowe's stores in Columbus, Mississippi and Gadsden, Alabama. The portfolio carries a weighted average remaining lease term of approximately seven years.

The Trust is capitalized entirely with $89,517,000 of equity and carries no debt. Proceeds are used to redeem Class 2 Beneficial Interests held by the Depositor. An affiliated Master Tenant holds the Master Lease and is capitalized through a Demand Note. The Operating Partnership holds a fair market value option to acquire Interests in exchange for OP Units in a transaction intended to qualify under Section 721; investors have the option to receive cash in lieu of Units.
notes:
The structural strengths are the balance sheet and the sponsor. There is no debt, so no refinancing, debt-service or rate exposure, and the sponsor is Apollo Global Management rather than a first-time syndicator.

The caution is duration. Weighted average remaining lease term is roughly seven years against a ten-year forecast, so a meaningful share of the portfolio hits renewal or re-leasing before the projected hold ends, and the distribution curve only climbs from 4.6% to 4.9% across the whole period. That is a flat return profile for taking single-tenant rollover risk in secondary markets — Muncie, Gadsden, Columbus — where re-tenanting a big-box store is not quick.

Tenant credit is solid: Kroger, Sam's Club, BJ's and Lowe's are all national operators, and the retail categories are genuinely distinct rather than nominally diversified. The 721 option preserves an investor cash election, which is the better of the two structures seen in this group.

name: Blue Door Property II DST
description:
Blue Door Property II DST is a $64.77 million, unlevered portfolio of three SmartStop-branded self-storage facilities in Orlando, Florida; Corinth, Texas; and Pasadena, Texas. The assets contain approximately 2,281 storage units and 98 vehicle-storage spaces, with reported physical occupancy of 91.2% as of May 31, 2025.

Each Operating Trust leases its property to an affiliated Master Tenant under a 10-year Master Lease, automatically renewable for up to three five-year terms unless the Master Tenant elects not to renew. The Trust can receive base rent plus additional and bonus rent; projected investor cash flow is 4.41% in Year 1 and 5.06% in Year 10. In an OP Transaction, investors may elect cash, OP units, or a combination; the OP-unit path is intended to qualify under Section 721.
notes:
This is a direct self-storage operating-income underwriting, not a lease guaranty credit. Cash flow depends on occupancy, achieved rental rates, expenses, and the affiliated Master Tenant’s ability to fund fixed base rent. The Master Tenant has limited capital and retains a share of property cash flow above prescribed thresholds; the Trust bears the risk that asset-level operating performance fails to cover fixed rent.

Unlevered capitalization removes forced-sale and interest-rate risk, but also leaves return entirely dependent on self-storage operating performance. Reported 91.2% occupancy is useful but not a long-term lease covenant, and the 10-year Master Lease contains tenant-controlled renewal elections. The optional 721 path is tied to an affiliated private, non-traded REIT and does not create committed liquidity.

name: Blue Door Property III DST
description:
Blue Door Property III DST is a $52.64 million self-storage capitalization consisting of three SmartStop-branded facilities: Phoenix, Arizona; Longwood, Florida; and Dallas, Texas. The portfolio contains approximately 1,927 storage units, 24 modular outdoor storage units, and 12 vehicle-storage spaces.

The Trust has $24.19 million of first-mortgage debt across three affiliate loans, with a 5.00% fixed rate, interest-only payments, and a November 13, 2032 maturity. The Master Tenants are Sponsor affiliates and remit lender-directed base rent plus any available additional and bonus rent. A potential OP Transaction permits each investor to elect cash, OP units, or a mix; the OP-unit path is intended to qualify as a Section 721 contribution.
notes:
The capital structure is the primary underwriting constraint: $24.19 million of interest-only debt equals 45.96% of total capitalization and matures in November 2032. The portfolio must either refinance, sell, or satisfy extension conditions at maturity; up to two one-year extensions reprice at SOFR + 150 bps. The 5.00% fixed coupon protects near-term debt service but creates a refinancing and valuation test at the balloon date.

Cash flow to investors is residual after lender-directed base rent. The Master Tenants are affiliated, limited-capital entities; they may retain part of upside but must cover operating shortfalls. Consequently, operating metrics at Phoenix, Longwood, and Dallas—not merely the stated 4.00%-4.25% distribution target—drive debt coverage and equity return. The optional 721 transaction remains a sponsor-controlled exit structure subject to appraisal and OP-unit valuation.

name: Blue Owl Real Estate Exchange V DST
description:
The Trust owns three industrial manufacturing campuses totaling approximately 2.34 million square feet in St. Marys, Ohio; Plymouth, Michigan; and Bowling Green, Kentucky. The Ohio and Michigan assets are occupied by American Rheinmetall affiliates, while the Kentucky facility is occupied by a Magna International subsidiary. The Trust has no property debt.

The assets are subject to a 20-year net Master Lease with a Blue Owl Operating Partnership affiliate. The Operating Partnership provides a full payment-and-performance guaranty. The Operating Partnership may exercise an FMV option after the required holding period; if exercised, holders are required to accept cash or OP units as determined by the Operating Partnership.
notes:
The principal credit is the Blue Owl Operating Partnership guaranty, not merely the end-tenant leases. The guaranty reduces direct tenant and operating volatility at the Trust level, but shifts underwriting to the balance-sheet capacity, liquidity, and incentive alignment of the affiliated Operating Partnership. The Master Lease is a related-party instrument and may constrain residual value because appraisal is taken subject to the Master Lease.

The portfolio is unlevered, which removes refinancing risk, but investor economics still depend on manufacturing demand, Magna's automotive-cycle exposure, Rheinmetall-related defense demand, and the guarantor's ability to perform through tenant disruption. The FMV option is sponsor-controlled: it can force a cash or OP-unit outcome after the holding requirement, and investors do not control timing or form of consideration.

CF Fleetwood Multifamily DST owns 42 Broad, a 249-unit multifamily residential community in the Fleetwood neighborhood of Mount Vernon, New York, in Westchester County. The Trust is capitalized with $74,900,000 of equity and a $75,949,000 Freddie Mac loan originated by Arbor Agency Lending, LLC at 50.35% of total capitalization, fixed at 5.09% to a July 1, 2036 maturity. The loan is interest-only for the full term with no amortization.

The property is subject to a net master lease with an affiliate of the Sponsor as Master Tenant, paying Base Rent, Additional Rent above a breakpoint and Bonus Rent above a second breakpoint. Cantor Fitzgerald Investors, LLC is the Sponsor. The offering funds $5,000,000 of Trust Reserves, the largest reserve allocation of the three Cantor Fitzgerald offerings reviewed.
notes:
The reserve position is the strongest of the three Cantor Fitzgerald deals — $5.8 million across Trust, Master Tenant and lender escrows, 7.7% of equity. Fixed-rate agency debt at 5.09% through 2036 removes rate risk for the full projected hold, and Westchester County multifamily is a defensible submarket. The loan is interest-only for the entire ten years, though, so there is no deleveraging and the full balance arrives at maturity.

The structural caution is the rent waterfall. Additional Rent Cash on Cash Return is pinned at 4.15% for all ten years. Every dollar of the climb from 4.25% to 6.01% comes from Bonus Rent, which is only paid above a breakpoint that rises each year, so the back half of the distribution curve is contingent on the property outperforming an escalating hurdle rather than on contracted rent.

The sponsor's own prior-performance disclosure deserves weight here. The PPM records prior Cantor Fitzgerald programs where distributions were cut from target: 5.12% to 3.00% in August 2020, 4.75% to 3.00% in September 2025, 4.25% to 3.00% in April 2026, and one program from 4.25% to 2.00% in November 2023 and then to 0.00% in August 2024. Against that history, a targeted 4.25% opening distribution on a Bonus-Rent-dependent curve warrants a hard look at the underlying operating assumptions.

The Trust acquired the property from an unaffiliated third party below its appraised value and is capitalized entirely with $107,600,000 of owner equity; there is no Trust-level debt. A July 31, 2026 appraisal by Partners Valuation Advisory supports that valuation, but it was prepared for an unaffiliated third party and expressly may not be relied upon by the Trust or the Owners.
notes:
The tenant credit is about as strong as net lease offers: Amazon.com, Inc. at S&P AA on a 2021-built distribution center with ten years of remaining term and four five-year options behind it. All cash, no leverage.

Three features separate this from ExchangeRight's usual product. It is a single building with a single tenant. The marketing leads with the REIT's 436 properties across 38 states and 44 tenants, but that diversification belongs to the vehicle investors exchange into, not to what they own during the hold. It is a double net lease rather than the absolute NNN structure the sponsor's retail portfolios use, so the Trust retains landlord obligations. The material question is not the two years of cash flow but whether the exchange into the Essential Income REIT occurs on the terms, timing and valuation described. As of the Memorandum date the Trust does not own the property; it holds a binding contract to acquire it from HPI Deer Creek LLC and HPI Deer Creek Land LLC, both Sponsor affiliates, with closing anticipated on or about September 15, 2026. The Loan remains in lender underwriting and the rate will be fixed shortly before closing at the 10-year Treasury plus 92 basis points. notes:
Two features separate this from most of the table. It is a pre-closing offering: as of the Memorandum date the Trust does not own Xenia Trails, closing is anticipated on or about September 15, 2026, the Freddie Mac CME loan remains in lender underwriting, and the rate is not fixed until shortly before closing at the 10-year Treasury plus 92 basis points. Exhibit E models 5.42% while the insert cites 5.47% against a 4.55 Treasury; every distribution figure in the forecast moves if the Treasury moves before the lock. And the seller is a Sponsor affiliate, HPI Deer Creek LLC and HPI Deer Creek Land LLC, so the price was not set at arm's length and the appraisal is the only independent check available.

The forecast leans on execution. Year 10 effective gross income is roughly 40% above Year 1, and the value-add income line grows from $60,840 to $561,600, carrying a meaningful share of the yield ramp, so the back half of the distribution curve is earned rather than contracted. Full-term interest-only means no deleveraging and a $25.3 million balloon in 2036 against 2036 cap rates. The offset is the sponsor: Hamilton Point has run eight prior multifamily funds with full-cycle liquidations and stated distributions of 6.25% to 8.00%, a materially longer record than most DST sponsors bring.

description:
Inland Long Island Residential DST owns The Arboretum, a 292-unit apartment community at 20 Maple Lane, Farmingville, New York, on Long Island. The property was built in 2023/2024 and comprises approximately 491,071 square feet of net leasable area across 227 two-bedroom and 65 three-bedroom units; 30 units are designated Affordable Housing Units under local law and the property participates in a New York PILOT program. Occupancy was 93% as of January 19, 2026. The Trust acquired the property from Brookhaven Residences LLC on January 30, 2026, capitalized with $107,581,888 of equity and a $104,500,000 PNC loan at 49.27% of total capitalization.

The loan is interest-only and floats at Daily Simple SOFR plus 1.25%, hedged by a rate cap through June 2029 and a forward swap fixing 5.382% from June 2029 through January 2036. An affiliated Master Tenant leases the property and pays Base Rent, Additional Rent above a breakpoint and Supplemental Rent above a second breakpoint. No 721 exchange option is offered; Section 721 appears in the Memorandum only in connection with a Transfer Distribution to a springing LLC if the Trust cannot dispose of the property before loan maturity.
notes:
Rejected. The asset itself is credible: new construction, Long Island infill, 93% occupied in lease-up. Coverage takes five of ten years, landing exactly on the Preferred/Common boundary.

The forecast is the deciding factor. Master Lease Base Rent is flat at $5,624,190 from 2027 while debt service climbs from $4.12 million to $5.62 million by 2030 as the rate cap steps from 4.30% to 4.90% and the swap takes over at 5.382%. Excess Base Rent is $1.04 million in 2026 and zero from 2030 onward, so the entire cushion between rent and debt service is consumed by the hedge schedule. Distributions stay pinned at 4.35% for four years and move only once Supplemental Rent clears a breakpoint that rises every year.

Combined with 30 rent-restricted Affordable Housing Units, New York PILOT compliance, a designated Hurricane Susceptible Region, and 49.27% leverage on floating debt that is only synthetically fixed, the margin for error is thin against a 4.35% current yield.

name: JLLX Industrial Portfolio DST
description:
JLLX Industrial Portfolio, DST holds five industrial buildings totaling 1,406,034 square feet of net rentable area across four markets, 100% leased to five different tenants: two adjacent buildings in Fremont, California totaling 237,312 square feet, one building in Chandler, Arizona, one in Jefferson, Georgia and one in Whitestown, Indiana.

The Trust is capitalized entirely with $253,383,866 of equity and carries no debt. The Sponsor, JLL Exchange TRS, LLC, is a taxable REIT subsidiary of JLLIPT Holdings LP. The Operating Partnership holds both a Portfolio FMV Option and a Real Estate FMV Option; if either is exercised, each Beneficial Owner is required to exchange its interest for OP Units in a transaction intended to qualify under Section 721, receiving OP Units with an aggregate value equal to the then fair market value of the Interests.
notes:
Rejected. The portfolio itself is genuinely attractive — no debt, an institutional sponsor with a real industrial platform, and five well-located buildings fully leased to five separate tenants, which is diversification of substance rather than of name.

The economics are what fail. A 4.11% year-one distribution is the lowest starting yield in the inventory, and the forecast runs only five years, reaching 4.96%. Investors are being asked to accept a sub-4.2% current return on $253 million of equity with no leverage to amplify it and no cash election at exit: both the Portfolio FMV Option and the Real Estate FMV Option require an exchange into JLLIPT OP Units if the Operating Partnership chooses to exercise. That combination — low current income, a short disclosed window, and a compulsory roll-up into a non-traded vehicle whose valuation the sponsor controls — means the investor's return depends almost entirely on the OP unit valuation at an exchange they cannot decline. A $14.75 million supplemental trust reserve is also held back at the Trust, further reducing the capital working in the real estate.

name: MDI Overland Park Net Lease DST
description:
MDI Overland Park Net Lease DST holds a 17,592-square-foot Caliber Collision automotive service facility on a 1.58-acre site at 14939 Metcalf Avenue, Overland Park, Kansas. The 2022 build-to-suit is absolute triple-net leased to Caliber Holdings, LLC for an initial 15-year term expiring July 31, 2038, with two five-year renewal options and a corporate guaranty from Wand Newco 3, Inc., the parent of Caliber Collision. Rent is currently $347,500 annually ($19.75/SF) with 10% increases every five years. The Trust completed the acquisition on July 29, 2026 and is capitalized entirely with equity at $6,657,515; there is no Trust-level debt.

The Sponsor's stated objective is a sale, disposition, 1031 exchange or Section 721 exchange no earlier than two years after completion of the Offering and within seven years. An FMV Option permits an affiliate to acquire investor interests in a transaction intended to qualify under Section 721; investors may elect cash instead of Equity Units, and the FMV Optionholder has sole discretion over whether to exercise. The PPM states it is anticipated the option would be assigned to an affiliated REIT operating partnership, and that no public market for the Interests or the Equity Units exists or is expected to develop.
notes:
The real estate case is clean: all-cash capitalization, an absolute NNN lease with zero landlord obligations, and roughly twelve years of remaining term. The exposures sit elsewhere. Income depends entirely on one privately held, Hellman & Friedman-owned tenant; the guaranty comes from Wand Newco 3, Inc., a holding company with no public financials, and the confidential S-1 filing is not a completed IPO. The building is a purpose-built collision-repair facility, which the PPM's own risk factors concede could mean substantial re-leasing costs or a lower sale price.

Rent escalations of 10% every five years are approximately 1.9% annually, and only one step falls inside the forecast period.

The 721 exit is the weakest part of the marketing. The PPM states the affiliated REIT operating partnership that would issue Equity Units has yet to develop, and MDI revoked its REIT election effective January 1, 2026, so the UPREIT path is a stated intention rather than an existing vehicle. Sponsor track record is short: this is Medalist's second DST, following a November 2025 inaugural offering that was 85.72% sold as of July 2026. Nasdaq listing, SEC reporting, a Cherry Bekaert audit and FactRight third-party review are real offsets, but they are governance rather than performance history.

Interest Rate is recorded as the 4.589% senior coupon, which carries roughly 92% of principal; the subordinated coupons are 7.870% and 10.756%. name: PREP Essential Net Lease I DST
description:
PREP Essential Net Lease I DST was formed to acquire a 65,223-square-foot Shaw's Supermarkets store at 160 Paine Turnpike North, Berlin, Vermont, with approximately 406 surface parking spaces. The building was purpose-built for Shaw's in 1996 and has been continuously occupied by the tenant since March 1997. Shaw's Supermarkets, Inc. is a subsidiary of Albertsons Companies, Inc. The lease is absolute net, relieving the Trust and Master Tenant of all operating obligations and capital expenditures including capital repairs, environmental and fire/casualty insurance. It expires December 31, 2039 with six five-year renewal options, and rent steps from $1,271,848 annually through 2029 to $1,373,596 for 2030-2034 and $1,483,484 for 2035-2039.

The Trust is capitalized entirely with $23,985,832 of equity and takes on no debt. The property was acquired below its November 30, 2025 as-is appraised value, with closing anticipated on or around March 18, 2026. The Initial Beneficiary funds the purchase in advance using a bridge loan from PECO Real Estate Partners Net Lease Income REIT, an affiliate of the Sponsor and the parent of the Seller; that bridge is repaid from Offering proceeds. An affiliated Master Tenant holds the Master Lease and PREP Co., LLC serves as Asset Manager.
notes:
The tenant is the strongest element: an Albertsons subsidiary occupying a purpose-built store for 29 years on an absolute net lease with no landlord obligations at all, not roof, structure or casualty, running to December 31, 2039 with six five-year options behind it. The asset was acquired below its November 2025 appraised value. All cash, so no refinancing or interest-rate exposure.

The questions concern who sits on the other side of the trade. The Seller is a wholly owned subsidiary of PECO Real Estate Partners Net Lease Income REIT, the Bridge Lender is that same REIT, and both are Sponsor affiliates, so one affiliate group owns the asset, lends the money to buy it from itself, and is repaid out of investor equity. A PREP affiliate has owned and managed the property since 2022, so the price is not arm's length and the appraisal is the only independent check, which came in above it. The Memorandum states plainly that the Sponsor is a newly formed entity with limited operating capital and no operating history, which matters because the Sponsor backs the Master Tenant through a Demand Note. Against that, Michael C. Phillips founded Phillips Edison & Company in 1991 and formed thirteen private funds there, so the principal-level record is real even where the sponsoring entity is not.

Economically the yield is thin and flat. The projected distribution rate is 5.00%, holding flat for five years before a single step to 5.25%. On a fourteen-year lease that is a bond-like return carrying grocery-anchor single-tenant risk and a 2039 residual.

name: Sealy Industrial I DST
description:
The Trust owns a 303,456-square-foot, 2024-built warehouse on 29.98 acres at 4210 West 67th Street in Anderson, Indiana. Pioneer Hi-Bred International, a Corteva subsidiary, leases the asset through December 2036 with two five-year options. EIDP, Inc., a Corteva subsidiary, guarantees the tenant's lease payment and performance obligations.

The property is offered without permanent mortgage financing. The PPM identifies no 721/UPREIT exit program. The financial forecast reports Funds Available for Distribution of $2.08 million in year 1, $1.88 million in year 2 and $2.20 million in year 9.
notes: This is a single-tenant, corporate-guaranteed industrial credit with no mortgage leverage, which reduces capital-structure risk materially. The effective economic risk is the Corteva/Pioneer credit and the re-leasing value of a 303,456-square-foot facility designed for the tenant's operations; a tenant default could force a Springing LLC conversion before the Trust can re-lease. The disclosed funds available for distribution equate to roughly 4.65%-5.44% of maximum equity during years 1-10.

name: Starboard Bradley DST
lender: Freddie Mac; originated and serviced by KeyBank
description:
The Banks on Bradley is a 144-unit, 2024-built garden-style multifamily property on 4.56 acres at 355 Bradley Boulevard in Richland, Washington. The community contains 105,516 net rentable square feet across studios, one- and two-bedroom units, with a clubhouse, pool, fitness center and pet spa.

The Trust acquired the property from a sponsor affiliate in a contribution transaction and financed it with a $19.30 million Freddie Mac loan. The property is master leased to Starboard Bradley MT, a wholly owned sponsor subsidiary; no 721/UPREIT exit program is identified.
notes: Leverage is modest, and the fixed 5.11% Freddie Mac loan removes near-term refinance risk. The Master Tenant is a wholly owned sponsor subsidiary with limited capital, not a corporate-guaranteed lease counterparty. Consequently, cash flow remains directly exposed to community occupancy, concessions, operating costs and Master Tenant performance. The forecast assumes 91.6% economic occupancy in year 1 while the market absorbs 593 new units in 2026; annual distributions decline to 4.41% in year 8 as debt begins amortizing.

name: Starboard Makley DST
lender: Freddie Mac; originated and serviced by Newmark (Berkeley Point Capital)
amort: Interest-only for 10 years; 30-year amortization schedule thereafter
description:
Makley Place is a mixed-use property at 210 West 5th Avenue in Columbus, Ohio, with 140 apartments in a six-story residential building and three ground-floor commercial suites. The apartment component totals 102,768 net rentable square feet and the commercial component totals 6,128 square feet. The Trust acquired the asset and financed it with a $23.68 million Freddie Mac loan.

The Trust leases the asset to Starboard Makley MT, a wholly owned sponsor subsidiary. A December 2025 supplement replaces the original forecast and adds a five-unit corporate-rental program plus a resident-protection-plan revenue stream. No 721/UPREIT exit program is identified.
notes: The asset combines urban multifamily and small-format commercial income with a fully interest-only 10-year Freddie Mac loan, avoiding amortization drag during the hold but leaving a $23.68 million balloon at maturity. The 52.6% LTV is acceptable against total capitalization. The updated forecast depends partly on five furnished corporate units and renter-insurance revenue, which are operational initiatives rather than contractual rent. The Master Tenant is sponsor affiliated and explicitly has limited capital; it is not an independent credit enhancement.
